title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. G is a reductive group, almost certainly GL_2: its centre is G_m, det: G -> G_m, and PG = PGL_2. M_{ρ,σ} is an auxiliary group scheme with a homomorphism Θ: M_{ρ,σ} -> G. On the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' pages it is built from a pair of elements ρ, σ with their tori T_ρ, T_σ. Θ̃ is the composite M -> G -> PG. In the modular case over Z, the subgroups T_ρ(Z) ≅ Z/6 and T_σ(Z) ≅ Z/4 are the stabilisers of the elliptic points of SL_2(Z).

This page opens §6°, 'groups attached to the radical', and fixes notation.
(86) The radical is defined as R_{ρ,σ} := Ker(Θ̃: M -> PG).
(87) This gives the exact sequence 1 -> R -> M -> PG -> 1, implicitly asserting that Θ̃ is surjective (fppf).
(88) R° := R ∩ M° (introduced at (69)) is identified with the neutral component of R.
(89) Equivalently, R = Θ^{-1}(G_m), since the kernel of G -> PG is the centre G_m.
(90) Θ restricted to R factors through the centre. This defines κ: R -> G_m, with Θ(g) = κ(g)·1 (the commutativity condition (91)). Hence the exact sequence 1 -> SR -> R -> G_m -> 1, with SR := Ker κ = Ker Θ.
(92) χ := det ∘ Θ: M -> G_m is the character introduced earlier at (57).
(93) For a point g of R one has χ(g) = det(κ(g)·I_2) = κ(g)^2. That is, χ|R equals κ followed by squaring.

Purpose. This is book-keeping for the next page, which gives a prism of cartesian and cocartesian squares SR ⊂ R ⊂ M over the neutral components SR° ⊂ R° ⊂ M°. The quotients there are μ2×μ2, G_m, PG and G. It also gives the exact sequence 1 -> ST_ρ×ST_σ -> R -> G_m×μ2×μ2 -> 1. The aim is to compute the 'radical' groups, e.g. R°(Z) ≅ Z/6×Z/4×{±1} on the previous page, in the analysis of the loop equation for SL_2/GL_2 representations of the modular group.
errors: Surjectivity of M -> PG in (87) is asserted, not proved on this page.
Surjectivity of κ: R -> G_m in (90) is asserted, not proved on this page.

The identification of R ∩ M° with the neutral component of R in (88) needs a connectedness argument (R ∩ M° connected and open in R). It is stated without justification. Grothendieck himself flags a related surjectivity check (onto μ2×μ2) in a margin note on the next page.
(93) presupposes G = GL_2 (det of a scalar λ is λ^2). This is consistent with the context but implicit.

ideas.what: Radical R = kernel of the projectivised homomorphism M -> PG, with exact sequences relating it to M, PG, G_m and SR = Ker Θ
ideas.modern_name: Kernel / extension book-keeping for group schemes; preimage of the centre
ideas.where_published: Not published; the specific groups M_{ρ,σ} belong to the unpublished 'équation des lacets' notes

ideas.what: Relation χ|R = κ^2, i.e. the determinant of a scalar in GL_2 is its square
ideas.modern_name: Determinant restricted to the centre of GL_2

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely notational and routine set-up of exact sequences for the radical of M_{ρ,σ}. Any interest lies in the broader unpublished 'loop equation' programme, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: Header: the crossed-out line reads roughly '6° Le sous-groupe M_{ρ,σ}(1/2?)', with '517' written above it. The marginal note reads 'Groupes associés au radical (R_{ρ,σ}, SR_{ρ,σ}, R°_{ρ,σ}, SR°_{ρ,σ} …)'.
(88): 'défini dans 69' annotates R°_{ρ,σ}, i.e. R° was defined in (69).

Line after (91): it reads 'Notons en passant que l'homom. χ de (92) M_{ρ,σ} -> G_m [déduit ci-dessus?] de Θ (57) par composition'. Here (57) is a reference to an earlier formula number, not a new formula label.
(93): 'g ∈ Γ R_{ρ,σ}' means g is a section (point) of R_{ρ,σ}. The commutative triangle is κ followed by λ ↦ λ^2, equal to χ|R_{ρ,σ}.
